160373.title: Spreadsheet: Vector column auto fit width issue when component values differ greatly
160373.feasibility_reason: The issue clearly identifies a UI layout problem in the spreadsheet where vector column widths are calculated from the concatenated string rather than individual component widths. However, without direct access to the codebase UI drawing/layout code for spreadsheet columns, locating the exact file requires searching.
160373.problem_summary: Spreadsheet vector/multi-component column auto-fit calculates column width by formatting the entire vector as a concatenated string. Because multi-component columns divide total space equally among components in the UI, an uneven distribution of component lengths (e.g. `1000000000, 0, 0`) leads to truncation of the widest component.
160373.root_cause_hypothesis: The column width estimation logic in the Spreadsheet editor (`estimate_max_column_width` or equivalent value-formatting calculation) evaluates the width of the whole concatenated string across components. When drawn, each sub-component gets an equal share of the column width (`total_width / num_components`), meaning the widest component requires `max(component_widths) * num_components` rather than `sum(component_widths)`.
160373.suggested_approach: Adjust the column width estimation logic for multi-component types (float2/3/4, int2/3, short2, color, quaternion) to measure the formatted string width of each component individually, find the maximum component width, and calculate the overall column width as `max_component_width * num_components` (plus any necessary spacing/margins).
prerequisites: A working Blender C++ development build environment.
Understanding of Blender's Spreadsheet editor column drawing and auto-fitting logic.
implementation_steps: Locate the column width estimation function in `source/blender/editors/space_spreadsheet/` (e.g., `estimate_max_column_width` or component drawing width calculation).
Identify how multi-component values (vectors, rotations, colors) are currently formatted and measured during column auto-fit.
Modify the measurement routine for composite data types to calculate the width of each individual sub-component string separately instead of measuring the concatenated vector string.
Set the estimated column component width to the maximum width found among all components multiplied by the component count, accounting for inter-component padding/separators.

Open the Spreadsheet editor, load a dataset with varying component lengths (e.g. `[1000000000, 0, 0]`), and double-click the column boundary to verify the auto-fit properly displays the longest component without truncation.
Test across various column data types (float3, int2, color, quaternion) and edge cases (negative values, standard float values) to ensure no regressions in layout or performance.
